transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-11
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55m
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Jonah Reed (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (HorizonHealth Procurement), Carlos Ruiz (HorizonHealth InfoSec), Leah Owens (HorizonHealth Legal), Marcus Lee (HorizonHealth CTO)

Auto-summary: quick alignment on MSA/DPA redlines, KMS and VPC options, SLA expectations. Agreed to legal deep dive and SE follow-up with PoC plan.

[00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we should be able to get through the scoping items in about 45 minutes and leave time for Qs. Uh, quick roll-call?
[00:12] Priya: Hi this is Priya, procurement, here.
[00:15] Carlos: Carlos here from security.
[00:18] Leah: Leah, legal. Marcus is on in a sec.
[00:22] Marcus: Sorry, car trouble, I'm on now, Marcus CTO.
[00:26] Maya: Great. Jonah from engineering on my side, he'll cover technical gating, perf, and the PoC plan.
[00:32] Jonah: Hey all.

[00:40] Maya: First item — MSA and DPA, Leah I think you sent some initial redlines? Can you summarize top concerns?
[00:48] Leah: Yeah, quick summary — main asks are clearer data processing terms for patient-adjacent data, stronger audit logging obligations, and a clause for data residency. Also we have a stub for KMS bring-your-own-key in the DPA but we want more specifics, like who controls keys, key rotation, and whether logs that reference keys are redacted.
[01:10] Maya: Got it. From Redwood's side we have a standard DPA with optional KMS integration for our private deployments; hosted customers can use our managed KMS with enterprise encryption but we can support customer-managed keys for Private or Dedicated. I will send our MSA + DPA markups.
[01:25] Leah: Can you confirm whether the hosted API uses customer-key isolation? We need to know if tokens or cache could leak across tenants.
[01:33] Jonah: Short answer: no cross-tenant leakage in normal operation — we use tenant isolation, namespace-level KV caches. That said, older notes in the doc might say, um, some caching layers are shared; for regulated workloads you should pick Dedicated or Private so KV caches and GPUs are isolated.
[01:52] Carlos: And what about logs? Are request logs encrypted at rest and is PII masked by default?
[01:58] Jonah: Logs are encrypted at rest. Request-level logs with PII are redacted in hosted by default; for Private we can turn off storing request logs entirely. We'll share the exact retention and redaction settings.

[02:15] Priya: On procurement side we need the MSA exceptions list and a pricing table — also our finance team needs annual commit scenarios.
[02:22] Maya: Absolutely. We'll include a hosted pricing sheet, Dedicated reserved capacity pricing with commit tiers, and a Private licensing quote. We'll also include overtime burst and ingress/egress estimates.

[02:35] Marcus: For SLA, our production use needs 99.95% availability and p50 latency under 200ms for short non-streaming requests. Is that achievable?
[02:44] Jonah: For Hosted API on our verified LLMs, p50 at 200ms is plausible for small prompts under optimized configs; p95 will of course be higher. For guaranteed p50/p95 you'll likely want Dedicated with pinned capacity and autoscale rules — we can architect for those SLOs.
[03:05] Marcus: What about cold-starts and KV cache warmup for chat sessions? We expect production traffic, erratic but critical.
[03:12] Jonah: We'll recommend warmup probes and prefix caching. For PoC we'll provision a small warm pool and show the delta.

[03:25] Leah: Are there indemnity/liability caps that are problematic? Our legal team usually asks for higher ceilings on security breach liability for PHI-ish data.
[03:35] Maya: Our standard cap is two times annual fees for certain claims but we can take notes and discuss exceptions — that typically requires exec legal approval. We'll surface options in the markup.

[03:48] Priya: Timeline question — what's realistic from contract to pilot to prod? We have a board deadline for a procurement decision end of February.
[03:56] Maya: If we move quickly on legal redlines and procurement sign-off, a four-week PoC can start mid-Jan, and production by late March if PoC meets acceptance. So your Feb board decision is tight but possible.
[04:10] Priya: Good, need to make sure finance sees numbers this week.

[04:18] Marcus: Security — Carlos will want an architecture diagram for VPC peering and KMS flow. If we do BYOK, we need HSM-backed keys and compatibility with our Azure Key Vault.
[04:30] Carlos: Right. Also need SOC2 scope, ISO certifications, and any third-party pen test reports.
[04:36] Jonah: We have SOC2 Type II and the report; ISO is in progress. Pen test summary is available. I'll attach those docs. For BYOK we support HSM-backed KMS via standard KMIP and cloud-provider integrators; there are integration notes.

[04:58] Leah: On data residency — our primary constraint: data must remain in EU for EU users. How does Redwood handle multi-region routing?
[05:06] Jonah: We can pin inference to region; requests from EU customers can be routed to EU-hosted inference nodes and logs kept in-region. For Private deployments you control the region entirely. We'll document traffic routing and any cross-border fallback behaviors.

[05:25] Marcus: Do you offer an on-prem appliance? Some teams prefer air-gapped for certain workloads.
[05:30] Maya: We do have Private on-prem packages but that is a larger engagement. For now the PoC could be in a VPC with customer-managed keys which usually satisfies compliance gating.

[05:45] Priya: On pricing approvals — what level of discount for a 12-month committed Dedicated seat do we need to enter into a purchase order?
[05:53] Maya: Typical tiers are starter commit, mid-tier, and enterprise. We can provide a pricing matrix; discounts scale with commit and usage patterns. I'll include representative numbers in the sheet.

[06:10] Leah: A practical question — retention periods for logs and model traces. Our legal requires 90 days for full request traces, but PII redaction must be enabled, and longer retention needs justification.
[06:22] Jonah: Default hosted trace retention is 30 days; we can extend to 90 for enterprise with an add-on. For Private you can configure retention yourself. We'll note default vs configurable settings.

[06:40] Carlos: What about audit logs and access controls? We need SSO/SAML + RBAC + key rotation logs. Also ISV access via service accounts — how are those managed?
[06:52] Jonah: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, fine-grained RBAC, and audit logs with who/what/when. Service accounts can be scoped with API keys and limited routes. Rotation can be automated via API.

[07:10] Marcus: Are there any hard blockers you typically see on the legal side?
[07:14] Maya: Typically indemnity caps, data residency assurances, and BYOK specifics. Sometimes customers want the provider to hold certain logs for longer or to provide tailored monitoring — those can be added to a schedule.

[07:28] Priya: For procurement gate, our checklist needs an on-contract SLA figure for availability and credits. How do credits work?
[07:36] Maya: Credits are pro-rated refunds based on monthly uptime percentage falling below thresholds. We'll include the exact formula. For enterprise deals it's negotiable within reason.

[07:50] Leah: On the DPA — can we get an explicit subcontractor list? We need to know storage and infra vendors.
[07:56] Jonah: Yes, we'll provide a redacted subcontractor list — core infra and cloud partners only.

[08:05] Priya: Next, PoC acceptance criteria — we want to validate latency under load, accuracy/regression vs your baseline model, and secure KMS integration with our vault.
[08:15] Jonah: We'll draft an acceptance criteria doc: performance targets (p50/p95), throughput (requests/sec under burst), functional tests for prompt fidelity, and KMS integration validation steps. We'll include sample prompts and datasets (anonymized).

[08:35] Marcus: On observability during PoC — we need traces, tokenized cost breakdown, and per-route latency histograms.
[08:42] Jonah: Redwood Console exposes token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards; we can also provide tracing hooks and short-lived read-only access for your SREs.

[08:58] Maya: Leah, since legal sent redlines, is there anything in particular in the MSA header we should flag?
[09:05] Leah: The main redlines are liability, termination for convenience notice period, and export control warranties. We'll annotate and expect Redwood comments.

[09:18] Maya: Okay, we'll return markups with rationale. Can we aim to send that by Wednesday?
[09:22] Leah: Yes, that works for us.

[09:30] Priya: Small question — procurement prefers a simple SOW for PoC with explicit deliverables and an exit criteria so we can close the P.O.
[09:38] Jonah: We'll draft a one-page SOW and acceptance checklist.

[09:45] Marcus: For the PoC infra, if we go Dedicated, what's the minimum capacity?
[09:50] Jonah: For typical embedding + chat workflows, two A10-equivalent GPUs for baseline testing; we can scale up on demand. For strict latency SLOs you'd want dedicated warm pools.

[10:08] Carlos: On encryption in transit — do you support TLS1.3 and mutual TLS for internal service-to-service auth?
[10:14] Jonah: Yes TLS1.3; mTLS can be enabled for private peered connections. We'll include the network diagram and cipher specs.

[10:30] Maya: A couple of quick clarifying Qs: Priya, what is your expected procurement lead time for a mid-tier dedicated commit?
[10:36] Priya: If legal and finance move quickly, 4-6 weeks, but that assumes limited redlines.

[10:44] Maya: Leah, for the indemnity ask — any flexibility threshold you can share?
[10:49] Leah: We'll flag the preferred number but we need Redwood proposals; it's usually a negotiation point.

[10:58] Jonah: I'll also run a short internal benchmark tomorrow and share rough token-costs for the workloads you described.

[11:06] Marcus: If we do a hybrid — hosted for non-sensitive workloads and private for PHI-ish workloads — is routing managed under a single account?
[11:14] Jonah: Yes you can have a single org with multiple projects and routing policies; policy-based routing can send requests to dedicated/private based on customer tags or endpoints.

[11:28] Priya: One more — billing model: monthly invoicing with net-30? We prefer net-30 but finance sometimes needs net-45.
[11:35] Maya: Standard is net-30, but enterprise billing terms can be negotiated. We'll note this for the commercial team.

[11:44] Leah: Any third-party export control concerns? We want to confirm no sanctioned-country processing.
[11:50] Jonah: We'll include export control language and ensure default routing excludes sanctioned regions unless explicitly enabled.

[12:02] Maya: Okay time check, we've got about 7 minutes left. Quick recap and next steps — Maya?
[12:08] Maya: Summary — Redwood will: 1) send MSA/DPA markups; 2) deliver pricing matrix and hosted vs dedicated vs private breakdown; 3) SE to send PoC SOW and perf plan; 4) provide SOC2/pen test and integration docs. HorizonHealth will: 1) circulate procurement timeline; 2) Leah to review markups and schedule legal deep-dive; 3) Carlos to supply KMS integration constraints. Any additions?
[12:35] Priya: That's correct.
[12:38] Marcus: Good.

[12:42] Maya: Great, we'll target the dates we discussed. I'll follow up with calendar invites for the legal deep dive and PoC kickoff. Thanks everyone.
[12:49] Leah: Thanks.
[12:50] Carlos: Thanks all.
[12:52] Meeting end.
